body.text: Middesk is a San Francisco B2B software company selling business-identity infrastructure — verifying businesses for financial-services onboarding, and filing state and federal registrations on their behalf. Its customers are banks, lenders and payments companies onboarding business accounts of their own. The product line is software and filing services: it does not lend, and it does not hold customer funds.

Identity is settled on every axis the registries can speak to. The submitted name and address both match state registrations, entity type is confirmed against the Delaware filing, and the company holds an active registration in at least one state including the state of its submitted address. There is no daylight between what was submitted and what the states hold.

Registration status reads mixed — active in some states, inactive in others — and that is ordinary housekeeping for a company registered across many of them rather than a sign of lapse. A business withdraws from a state it no longer operates in; the pattern only matters if the inactive one is the state of operation, and here it is not.

gaps.point: Standing in Delaware, and the status of several registrations that returned nothing at all
gaps.wouldAnswer: Delaware publishes no good-standing sub-status for any company, so no order will produce it — a Certificate of Good Standing from the customer is the only route. Separately, the formation-state status and several others came back unresolved rather than negative, which a re-run of the registration search may clear.

body.text: A submitted person matches an officer named on a state registration — the strongest control-person evidence registry data produces, since it ties a named individual to a filing the state itself holds rather than to anything the customer supplied. For an operating company of this age that is the expected result and it is what the file has.

gaps.point: Whether the person named on the website is the person submitted
gaps.wouldAnswer: The website person check came back unverified — the site does not name them in a form the check could match. The officer match on the state registration already covers this ground more authoritatively, so the gap costs nothing here.
gaps.noAction: the officer match on the state registration covers this ground more authoritatively.

gaps.point: Who ultimately owns or benefits from the business
gaps.wouldAnswer: No beneficial-ownership insight exists in the catalog; ownership is only ever implied from the people filings happen to name. Officer is not owner. If your policy requires a UBO determination it cannot be satisfied from this record by any order.

body.text: It is visibly operating rather than merely registered. The address is commercial and deliverable, the website is reachable, and the domain registrant corroborates the business at high confidence, with the site's own name and address matching what was submitted. For account opening that combination does most of the work: registry data proves an entity exists, and this is what shows someone is running it.

Five addresses on the record are each shared with more than a hundred other businesses, which reads as a shell pattern only if you do not know what you are looking at. It is the expected shape of registered-agent addresses for a company registered in many states, and the connections on file are consistent with that rather than with a mass-registration cluster.

Screening is clean where it matters most. Watchlist and PEP returned no hits, no prohibited industry was identified, and there are no bankruptcy filings. Adverse media returned hits the provider itself scored low, which is worth an analyst's glance rather than an escalation.

Open liens were found and litigation records were returned. This is the only thing on the record that points at the business rather than at the limits of the data, and it is what the decision should turn on.

gaps.point: What the liens and litigation actually are
gaps.wouldAnswer: The record establishes that they exist and stops there — no amounts, no dates, no indication of whether they are satisfied. Ordering the lien and litigation detail is the single thing standing between this file and a decision.
